title: N01. A valuation makes the square small
N02. Sample digits at exponentially growing places
statement: A decimal expansion represents a rational number in $(0,1)$. Form a new decimal by taking its digits in positions $2,4,8,16,\ldots$. Prove that the new number is rational (possibly an endpoint such as zero).

title: N03. One modulus replaces all moduli
statement: Integers $b,n>1$ satisfy: for every integer $k>1$, some integer $a$ has $a^n\equiv b\pmod k$. Prove that $b$ is an integer $n$th power.

title: N04. Multiply three divided differences
statement: For positive integer $n$, prime $p$, and arbitrary integers $a,b,c$, suppose $a^n+pb=b^n+pc=c^n+pa$. Prove $a=b=c$.

title: N05. Simultaneous factorial valuations
statement: For any positive integer $d$ and finitely many primes $p_1,\ldots,p_k$, show that infinitely many $n>0$ satisfy $d\mid v_{p_i}(n!)$ for every $i$.

title: N06. Finite agreement versus eternal agreement
statement: Call an integer balanced when its number of prime factors, counted with multiplicity, is even; include $1$. (a) Find distinct positive $a,b$ for which $(n+a)(n+b)$ is balanced for all $1\le n\le50$. (b) Prove that if this holds for every positive $n$, then $a=b$.

title: N07. Divisibility squeezes a function
statement: Find all $f:\mathbb Z_{>0}\to\mathbb Z_{>0}$ satisfying $m^2+f(n)\mid mf(m)+n$ for all positive $m,n$.

title: N08. Two primes eliminate a factorial
N09. A cubic equation collapses to a short list
N10. Polynomial-root closure fills the integers
statement: A set $S\subseteq\mathbb Z$ contains $2^a-2^b$ for all positive $a,b$ and contains every integer root of every nonconstant polynomial with coefficients in $S$. Prove $S=\mathbb Z$.

title: N11. Classify the good binomial indices
statement: For fixed positive $a$, call $b>0$ good if $an+1\mid\binom{an}{b}-1$ whenever $an\ge b$. If $b$ is good and $b+2$ is not, prove $b+1$ prime.

title: N12. A Jacobi-symbol obstruction
statement: Show $2^n+65$ never divides $5^n-3^n$ for positive integer $n$.

title: N13. Reverse the ordered divisor list
statement: Let $1=d_1<\cdots<d_k=n$ be all positive divisors of a composite $n$. Classify $n$ for which $d_i\mid d_{i+1}+d_{i+2}$ for $1\le i\le k-2$.

title: N14. The odd part controls all divisors
statement: Find positive $n$ such that every divisor $d$ of $n$ has either $d+1\mid n$ or $d+1$ prime.

title: N15. Vieta jumping with every inequality checked
statement: For positive integers $a,b$ with $ab+1\mid a^2+b^2$, prove that $(a^2+b^2)/(ab+1)$ is a perfect square.

title: N16. Arithmetic descent in a nonlinear recurrence
statement: Start at an integer $a_0>1$. Replace a square by its positive square root and replace a nonsquare by that number plus three. Determine which initial values cause some integer to occur infinitely often.
